stem: (Select TWO.) At Corvid Analytics, an `aws_instance` resource's own configuration references a separate security group resource, so the instance depends on that security group. One engineer runs `terraform destroy -target aws_instance.example`; another instead deletes the instance's resource block from the configuration and runs `terraform apply`, leaving the security group's block untouched. Which two statements accurately compare what happens?

choices.text: destroy -target on the instance also destroys the security group it depends on, in the same run
Deleting only the instance's block and applying leaves the security group resource exactly as it was
Both routes end with only the instance destroyed and the security group left untouched, no matter which target was named
This targeted destroy only ever removes the exact resource named on the command line, never anything it depends on
Deleting the instance's block and running `terraform apply` also destroys the security group that the instance depended on

rationale: destroy -target extends to whatever the targeted resource depends on, so the security group is destroyed along with the instance in one run; deleting only the instance's block and applying does not touch the security group at all, since plan only proposes destroying what the edited configuration no longer describes. The two routes therefore do not end with the same result here, because the instance has a dependency. destroy -target is not limited to the exact named resource alone. The block-deletion route does not cascade the other way either: plan proposes destroying only the object the edited configuration stops describing, not anything that object depended on.
